primary_sources.citation: H. Araki and E. J. Woods, A Classification of Factors, Publ. RIMS Kyoto Univ. 4 (1968) 51-130, DOI 10.2977/prims/1195195263
primary_sources.establishes: infinite tensor products of Type-I factors can yield hyperfinite Type-II and Type-III factors; asymptotic ratio data determine the factor class in the classified cases

primary_sources.citation: A. Connes, Une classification des facteurs de type III, Ann. Sci. ENS 6 (1973) 133-252
primary_sources.establishes: Type-III classification through modular invariants; finite-dimensional Type-I behavior is insufficient to infer the continuum factor type

smallest_missing_inputs: a specified infinite sequence of local algebras/states or mode Hamiltonians beyond the four frozen frequencies
explicit embeddings or another precise construction relating successive finite algebras
state compatibility/convergence in a declared topology or GNS representation
a continuum modular-flow/cocycle domain and a type-discriminating invariant such as the asymptotic ratio/Connes spectrum
forbidden_inferences: do not extrapolate Type-III behavior from residual trends in m=2,3,4
do not infer impossibility of Type III merely because every finite truncation is Type I
do not choose a Powers/Araki-Woods limit post hoc without deriving it from the frozen physical regulator
